editorial:
Imagine taking a stroll through the old streets of New York with two legends of poetry. You get to watch István Eörsi, a Hungarian writer and activist, reunite with his old pal Allen Ginsberg. The vibe is super relaxed and feels like you are just hanging out with two old friends who have seen it all. They walk around the Lower East Side, joking around and reading their poems aloud. It is not a movie with a big plot or loud explosions, but it captures a very special bond between two creative souls who truly respect each other.

What really stands out is how natural the conversations feel. You see a side of Ginsberg that is warm and humble, which is great since this was filmed right before he passed away. The pacing is slow, so if you want a thriller, this isn't it. But if you like people-watching and hearing deep thoughts about life, you will love it. It is a perfect pick for a rainy Sunday.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with the two friends continuing their walk and sharing final thoughts on art and politics. There is no big twist because it is a real-life documentary. It ends on a bittersweet note as they say their goodbyes. Knowing that Ginsberg died shortly after these scenes makes the final moments feel very precious. You leave the film feeling a sense of peace and a deep appreciation for their lifelong friendship.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves art, history, and genuine human connections.
